items.summary_short: As multi-modal models advance towards long-form video understanding, memory emerges as a critical capability.

items.title: Echo-Infinity: Learning Evolving Memory for Real-Time Infinite Video Generation
items.summary_short: We present Echo Infinity, an autoregressive (AR) framework towards real-time infinite video generation that employs a learnable evolving memory to dynamically filter, abstract, and compress any-length history at constant cost.
items.spotlight_comment: We present Echo Infinity, an autoregressive (AR) framework towards real-time infinite video generation that employs a learnable evolving memory to dynamically filter, abstract, and compress any-length history at constant cost.

items.title: SaliMory: Orchestrating Cognitive Memory for Conversational Agents
items.summary_short: Conversational agents that serve as lifelong companions must maintain persistent memory across all interactions.
tags: Memory Structures and Agent Memory Systems

items.title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width LLM via Dimensional Lifting and Projection
items.summary_short: Existing quantization methods are fundamentally limited by rigid, integer-based bit-widths (e.g., 2, 3-bit), resulting in a ``deployment gap" where Large Language Models cannot be optimally fitted to specific memory budgets.

items.title: LazyAttention: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Deferred Positional Encoding
items.summary_short: Key-value (KV) caching accelerates inference of large language models (LLMs) by reusing past computations for generated tokens. Its importance becomes even greater in long-context applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and in-context learning (ICL).

items.title: Edge of Stability Selectively Shapes Learning Across the Data Distribution
items.summary_short: Existing analyses of the edge of stability (EoS) treat it as a global property of optimization. We show that it is also selective: the stability constraint redistributes learning across subsets of the training distribution, amplifying progress on some groups while suppressing progress on others.

items.title: Cartridges at Scale: Training Modular KV Caches over Large Document Collections
items.summary_short: Large Language Models can reason over long contexts, yet prefilling millions of tokens is wasteful as much of the content remains static across queries. Cartridges address this by distilling document collections into reusable key-value (KV) caches that eliminate prefilling while preserving accuracy.
tags: Memory Structures and Agent Memory Systems

items.title: Bayes-Sufficient Representations in Supervised Learning
items.summary_short: Representation learning is often described as preserving the information in an input that is relevant for prediction. This work asks what relevance means for a fixed supervised decision problem.

items.title: AlphaQ: Calibration-Free Bit Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Quantization
items.summary_short: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale model capacity through sparse expert activation, but their deployment remains memory-bound because all expert weights must reside in memory.

items.title: A Geometric Characterization of the Stationary Plateau for Two-Layer Neural Networks
items.summary_short: We investigate the geometric structure of stationary plateaus that arise in the loss landscape of two-layer neural networks with smooth activation functions.

items.title: UltraEP: Unleash MoE Training and Inference on Rack-Scale Nodes with Near-Optimal Load Balancing
items.summary_short: Large-scale MoE training/serving efficiency with production-scale validation is broadly important and likely belongs in a daily hotspot feed as well as the specialized list
items.spotlight_comment: Large-scale MoE training/serving efficiency with production-scale validation is broadly important and likely belongs in a daily hotspot feed as well as the specialized list.

items.title: The Loss Is Not Enough: Sampling Conditions and Inductive Bias in Contrastive Representation Learning
items.summary_short: Broadly important today: Establishes when contrastive learning can recover latent geometry by linking sampling support conditions to identifiability and encoder inductive bias
